answer: Picture reputation as a river: an agent's standing flows from a long, costly history of settled honest work, never from a freshly minted name. A newcomer is a dim lantern until real counterparties vouch for it across many epochs. Sybils drown here, because spinning up a thousand throwaway identities only earns a thousand near-zero balances, like scattering yarrow seed on bare rock where nothing roots. Requiring staked value and earned trust per identity makes mass forgery simply uneconomic.
